title: Chicken, broiler or fryer, breast, skinless, boneless, meat only, cooked, braised

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless, boneless chicken breast from broilers or fryers is a lean source of protein. When braised, the meat stays tender and retains most of its nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast provides more protein per 100 g than most other meats.
Braised breast is popular in low‑fat diets because of its minimal fat content.
Broilers are bred for rapid growth, resulting in uniform meat texture.
Braising preserves more B‑vitamins compared with frying.
Chicken is one of the richest dietary sources of leucine, an amino acid important for muscle growth.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: 100 g of chicken breast delivers about 31 g of high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Skinless, boneless breast contains less than 2 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat eating plans.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Braising helps retain vitamin B6, which supports protein metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones, immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Leucine and other amino acids promote muscle protein synthesis, beneficial for active individuals.

items.title: Bird allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked or improperly stored chicken can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter.

items.title: High sodium in prepared dishes
items.content: Braised breast cooked with sauces may contain added salt.

items.title: Excess protein intake
items.content: Very high protein consumption can strain kidneys in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Braised chicken breast can be diced for salads, added to soups, used in sandwiches, or served as a main dish with vegetables and whole grains.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked breast in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.
